evals.name: classification-evidence-and-collisions
evals.prompt: Dry run only: classify four sanitized observations for GET /catalog/items. Existing not-found has codes [1004], http [200], and 200.code1004.not-found.json; its body says the item is missing. Frame A is a complete HTTP 404 capture, no business code, same missing-item meaning, captured 2026-09-28T01:00:00Z, no bodyMeta. Frame B is another HTTP 200/code 1004 capture with different request query and body than the existing file, no bodyMeta; its message confirms the same missing-item meaning. Frame C is HTTP 200/code 0 with response.body as JSON text and response.bodyMeta {representation: text, source: text, mimeType: application/json}; its message explicitly says the item was retrieved successfully, and glossary ok means successful retrieval; the current example schema supports bodyMeta. Frame D is HTTP 200/code 78123 with an unexplained opaque message. Give per-frame decisions, exact filenames where applicable, proposed mutations and unresolved items; do not execute CLI commands or edit repository data.
evals.expected_output: Merge A into not-found using its HTTP-only filename; preserve B alongside the existing example using a stable recording suffix; import C into ok while retaining JSON text and metadata; leave D unclassified. Keep existing identifiers and filenames stable and report partial completion for D.
assertions: Merges frame A into not-found with 404.http-only.not-found.json, retains code 1004 and adds HTTP 404.
Preserves the existing recording and filename for B, adds B with a stable recording suffix under not-found, and references both without renaming the semantic variant.
Imports C into ok using supported bodyMeta, preserving the original stored JSON text and metadata rather than parsing it into an object.
Leaves D unclassified and the glossary unchanged because code 78123 alone does not establish response meaning.
Reports unresolved frames and pending validation, and marks the import as incomplete.

evals.name: pipeline-recovery-on-windows
evals.prompt: Dry run only: give an executable recovery plan for importing sources/capture one.har and sources/capture two.har on Windows PowerShell. The CLI has not been built or linked. The working tree has unrelated edits. A previous extract stopped because .raw/GET.catalog.items.yaml was modified; no valid manifest owns that file. Only local results were requested. Assume classification later reports one frame with response.bodyMeta.source missing and no captured response body while other frames can be imported. State commands, working directories, handoffs, failure handling and completion criteria. Include how to check rendering stability when generated files are untracked. Do not run the pipeline or edit repository data.
evals.expected_output: Build and invoke the local CLI, supply explicit quoted HAR paths as one batch, choose fresh --out and pass it to classify, preserve unrelated work, report partial import for the missing response body, compare paths and hashes across two renders, keep delivery local.
assertions: Builds the pinned toolchain and invokes its CLI from the application root with --root ., passing both spaced HAR paths as one batch.
Uses a fresh --out directory and passes that directory to classify, preserving the modified draft and manifest.
Preserves unrelated changes and keeps delivery local without creating a PR.
Compares generated file paths and content hashes across consecutive renders, including untracked files.
Reports partial completion for the missing response body even if the remaining corpus checks pass; does not invent a response or discard its metadata.

evals.name: drift-adjudication-and-notes
evals.prompt: Dry run only: assess a drift report, then draft short Chinese endpoint notes; do not apply any canonical edits. The report labels HTTP 404/code 1004 as breaking for catalog.item-details. Existing not-found has HTTP 200/code 1004; complete sanitized examples establish identical missing-item meaning in both status-code combinations. Another change is a field absent in one sample (BodyNode has no required contract). A third reports data.id changing number to string, but the underlying capture is unavailable. The CLI exited 0. For notes, definition auth is optional, query itemId default is 42 (an observed value), access-denied has schema null and HTTP 403, and request cookies include {{SESSION_ID}}. Give one decision per change, version implications, then the proposed notes.md text using only behavior supported by the supplied evidence.
evals.expected_output: Classify the additional status-code combination as non-breaking; treat single-sample field absence as advisory; defer the type-change assessment until capture evidence is available. Keep versions unchanged in analysis mode and assess the report independently of exit code 0. Notes explain observed defaults, optional authentication, unavailable body structure and masked credentials.
assertions: Classifies the additional status-code combination as non-breaking based on confirmed shared meaning, retaining the existing semantic variant.
Treats one missing field as advisory without deleting the existing schema field.
Defers the unsubstantiated type-change judgment, keeps analysis read-only, and does not treat CLI exit 0 as absence of drift.
Explains that itemId default is an observed value and authentication is optional; keeps unsupported login or retry behavior unspecified.
Explains schema null as untrusted/unavailable shape and the cookie placeholder as masked, not a usable credential.
